newsitem.title: JAPAN: Prosecutors say Nomura director had racketeer ties.
newsitem.headline: Prosecutors say Nomura director had racketeer ties.

text.p: Japanese prosecutors said on Tuesday that a director at Nomura Securities illegally paid 38 million yen ($309,000) to a company run by a relative of a racketeer to avoid disruption of one of Nomura's annual shareholders' meetings.

It is the first time that authorities have linked the official to racketeers since the company said on March 6 that two directors had made discretionary deals banned under Japanese law and funnelled profits to a corporate client.

The allegation came shortly after a raid on Nomura's main offices and 10 other unspecified locations by prosecutors and officials from the nation's securities watchdog, the Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission (SESC).
Deputy chief prosecutor Kunihiro Matsuo said the former Nomura director accused of making the payment, Shimpei Matsuki, had not been detained.

He declined to comment on future plans regarding Matsuki and another former director, Nobutaka Fujikura. Nomura said on March 10 that Matsuki and Fujikura had been involved in irregular dealings and it had accepted their resignations.
Japanese racketeers, known as "sokaiya", extort money from companies by threatening to disrupt annual shareholder meetings. Paying off such racketeers is illegal.
